name: Occipital Lobe
summary: Almost entirely dedicated to vision. Processes edges, color, motion, depth, and shape recognition.

connections.note: The 'where/how' pathway — locates objects and guides action.

facts.text: About 30% of the entire cortex is devoted to vision — more brain territory than any other sense.
Damage to V4 causes cerebral achromatopsia — seeing only in grayscale. Damage to V5 causes akinetopsia — the world appears as frozen snapshots.

detailedDescription: The occipital lobe sits at the very back of the head. V1 (Primary Visual Cortex) receives raw retinal input and processes edges, orientations, and contrast. Visual information from the left visual field is processed in the right occipital lobe, and vice versa. Information flows forward through two major pathways: the ventral stream to the temporal lobe for object identification, and the dorsal stream to the parietal lobe for spatial processing.
